outcomeNote: A short string of dicta on the conduct of prayer; nothing is questioned, attacked or decided.

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אַל יִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם אֶלָּא בְּבַיִת שֶׁיֵּשׁ שָׁם חַלּוֹנוֹת. שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וְכַוִּין פְּתִיחָן לֵיהּ בְּעִלִּיתֵהּ (לָקֳבֵל) [נֶגֶד] יְרוּשְׁלֶם״.
segments.en: «And» on the topic of prayer, «Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Abba said» that «Rabbi Yoḥanan said: One may only pray in a house with windows,» as then he can see the heavens and focus his heart, «as it is stated» with regard to Daniel’s prayer: “In his attic «there were open windows» facing Jerusalem” (Daniel 6:11).

segments.he: אָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: חֲצִיף עֲלַי מַאן דִּמְצַלֵּי בְּבַקְתָּא.
segments.en: With regard to the appropriate place to pray, «Rav Kahana said: I consider impudent one who prays in a field.»

segments.he: וְאָמַר רַב כָּהֲנָא: חֲצִיף עֲלַי מַאן דִּמְפָרֵשׁ חִטְאֵיהּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַשְׁרֵי נְשׂוּי פֶּשַׁע כְּסוּי חֲטָאָה״.
segments.en: Employing parallel language, «Rav Kahana also said: I consider impudent one who specifies his transgression, as it is stated: “Happy is he whose iniquity is forgiven, whose transgression is covered over”» (Psalms 32:1); one who conceals his transgressions indicates that he is ashamed of them, and due to his shame he will be forgiven.

moves.cueHe: ואמר רבי חייא בר אבא אמר רבי יוחנן
moves.summary: the opening ו continues a run of R' Ḥiyya bar Abba–R' Yoḥanan dicta begun before this unit; one may pray only in a house with windows
moves.about: R' Yoḥanan's ruling that one may pray only in a house that has windows

moves.summary: Daniel's windowed attic is adduced as the prooftext
moves.about: Daniel's attic with open windows facing Jerusalem as the prooftext for praying in a house with windows

moves.cueHe: אמר רב כהנא: חציף עלי מאן דמצלי בבקתא
moves.summary: Rav Kahana calls one who prays in an open field impudent — a further dictum on the place of prayer

moves.cueHe: ואמר רב כהנא: חציף עלי מאן דמפרש חטאיה
moves.summary: a parallel dictum of Rav Kahana, strung to the first by its identical formula
moves.about: the verse praising one whose transgression is covered over, as the ground for not specifying one's sins

moves.summary: Psalms 32:1 is adduced for concealing rather than specifying transgression
